earlier_scan.source_named: Mouchet, Jean. 1958. Contribution a l'etude du Gula (Tchad) - grammar sketch per Glottolog; also Boyeldieu & Palayer 1975 Les langues du groupe Boua: Etudes phonologiques; neither online

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2017. La langue bolgo du Guéra (Tchad): Notes de recherche et matériel lexical. IFEAS Arbeitspapiere 172. Mainz.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Uses Jim Roberts' unpublished Bon Gula data for lexical comparison only; no Bon Gula prosody, no stress/accent anywhere.

tone.says: Held text checked: Bolgo is given a three-level tone system ('le bolgo a un systeme tonal de trois niveaux distinctifs'), with notes that tone marking in the sources is often missing; nothing is said about Bon Gula tone - Bon Gula forms serve lexical comparison only.
tone.citation_as_reported: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2017. La langue bolgo du Guéra (Tchad): notes de recherche et matériel lexical. Arbeitspapiere des Instituts für Ethnologie und Afrikastudien der Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz (AP IFEAS) 172. Mainz.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Personal pronouns in Bua languages. Language in Africa 1(3): 292-335. (HAL halshs-03097103)
sources.note: §9 Bon Gula pp. 315-319 (from Roberts 2004, 2010): 'Bon Gula sources consist of two SIL working papers that still contain some unsolved analyses and inconsistent transcriptions.' Pronoun paradigms only; the single 'syllable stress' remark (p. 301) concerns Tun, not Bon Gula.

sources.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2025. Multilingualism, identity, and language endangerment in southern Chad: the case of the Middle Chari area. In Gutova & Korangy (eds.), Handbook of Multilingualism, Identity, and Language Endangerment in Africa, 441-477. Springer (author's final draft).
sources.note: No mention of Bon Gula, stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent = 0).

sources.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2021. Areal alignment and the diversification of Bua languages (Chad). Slides, Diedrich Westermann Workshop, HU Berlin, 4-6 Nov 2021.
sources.note: Recent comparative phonology of the Bua group by the only linguist currently doing Bua fieldwork; could contain a prosodic typology row for Bon Gula (stem-initial prominence). PDF sits behind an Anubis bot-check on the HU Berlin site.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, P., R. Kastenholz, U. Kleinewillinghöfer & F. Lionnet. 2020. The Bua Group noun class system: looking for a historical interpretation. Language in Africa 1(3): 181-215.
sources.note: Bon Gula plural alternations (-l/-n, vowel changes) only; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2018. The Bua Group languages (Chad, Adamawa 13): A comparative perspective. In R. Kramer & R. Kießling (eds.), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages (AuÜ Beiheft 34), 53-126. Köln: Köppe.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|prominen = 0). Bon Gula data come from Roberts' unpublished 2004 wordlist (p. 59); §4.4 Tones pp. 71-72 characterises Ɓa, Lua, Tun, Bolgo (3 heights) and Kulaal (2 tones) but not Bon Gula; §5.5 p. 97: Bon Gula (Roberts 2004) added to tone Tables 21-22 'but.. it is still difficult to derive clear information from sources that are relatively limited and not systematically marked for tones, so that we will in fact not comment on them here'. Table 21 p. 98: Bon Gula noun tone reflexes H, H/HL, LH? with many '?'. Refere…

sources.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2017. Stem-initial prominence in West and Central Africa: Niger-Congo, areal, or both? Slides, ACAL 48.
sources.note: Bua languages listed under Middle-Chari stem-initial prominence are Lua and Ɓa only; Bon Gula not covered.

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 1988. Présentation sommaire du groupe boua (Tchad). In Barreteau & Tourneux (eds.), Le milieu et les hommes (Méga-Tchad 2), 275-286. Paris: ORSTOM.
sources.note: 'goula de Bon' appears only in the group inventory; the phonology remarks (3-register tone) cover Tun, Lua and Ɓa. No accent statement for Bon Gula.

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Bon Gula language' and 'Bua languages' (further-reading lists Mouchet 1958 and Faris & Meundeung 1993 'Etude sociolinguistique de la langue bon goula', SIL Chad, at a dead sil.org URL).
sources.note: No linguistic content on Bon Gula; the Internet Archive has no snapshot of the SIL PDF (availability API checked).

sources.citation: Roberts, Jim. 2010. Esquisse de grammaire Bone Goula. Mongo: SIL Tchad. Unpublished ms., 11 pp.

sources.note: Second SIL working paper on Bon Gula, main source of Boyeldieu 2020 §9; may restate the phonology including tone/accent.

sources.citation: Roberts, Jim. 2004. Notes on Bon Gula. Mongo: SIL Tchad. Unpublished ms., 26 pp.

sources.note: The main modern first-hand source (wordlist + phonological notes incl. ATR harmony, p. 1) used by Boyeldieu et al. 2018 and Boyeldieu 2020; an SIL working paper of this kind usually has a suprasegmentals section. Circulated privately by the author.

sources.citation: Faris, David & Marba Meundeung. 1993. Etude sociolinguistique de la langue bon goula. N'Djaména: SIL.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL Chad survey with a wordlist (formerly athttp://www.sil.org/Africa/Cameroun/bydomain/survey/reports/bongoula_faris1993_1920_p.pdf,now dead; no archived copy at the Internet Archive). Wordlist transcription might show tone/accent marking; low chance of a prosodic statement.

tone.says: Record + abstract + TOC only: 1993 SIL sociolinguistic survey (bilingualism, lexicostatistics, group interviews, questionnaires) with an annexed 'Liste de mots bon goula'; no phonology chapter in the TOC, so at most tone marks in the wordlist transcription; tone system not described as far as seen.
tone.citation_as_reported: Faris, David & Marba Meundeung. 2025 [1993]. Étude sociolinguistique de la langue bon goula du Tchad. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2025-001, 1-24. SIL Global (ISSN 2766-9327).
